record_notes.DCP-LETT-1410: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. P1–3 were composed Tuesday April 22, then the note returned because Malvern was omitted from the address. P4–5 were added Wednesday April 23. Tuesday explicitly answers the two Monday letters 1408 and 1408A; bowel action and Catherine concern specifically match 1408. Optimism precedes later deterioration news. Tuesday composition does not establish Tuesday availability to Darwin, and later receipt is unproved. Chloroform preparation concerns Emma impending confinement, not Annie treatment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1411: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Wednesday April 23 before-post P1–3 reread Monday 1408, explicitly recall vinegar sponging, offer foods tentatively, discuss family support, quote Caroline and report Willy and Franky. After-post P4 abruptly shifts to distress after Fanny April 22 deterioration letter, reproduced in footnote 7; it is not acknowledgement of Darwin same-day death notice 1412. Preserve the original Tuesday 21st dating variant and editorial correction to April 22. Fanny reports Darwin withheld an optimistic Tuesday letter; do not invent a sent source. Final pencil text ends unfinished after dear F. Historical family and medical reports remain attributed source material.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1412: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Wednesday April 23 announces Annie death at noon, peaceful passing, a short happy life, gratitude for the photograph, and mutual support for Emma. Darwin is unwell and return timing remains uncertain. Hope that Fanny note prepared Emma does not establish receipt of Emma 1410 or 1411 that day. No supported incoming prompt. Daguerreotype date and later frontispiece details are editorial apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1414: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Thursday April 24 before noon starts with mourning inferred from the absence of a promised improvement message and asks about the withheld optimistic letter known through Fanny. Earlier grief does not prove prior reading of 1412. Return hopes also draw on Fanny Wednesday six PM letter; 1412 does not promise an exact departure. P3 adds Willy reaction. No Darwin reading of this Emma response is established.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography.
